nodes.name: CCH/ZIF-67
aliases: ZIF-67 on the top of CCH nanoneedle arrays

nodes.name: Hydrothermal CCH synthesis
nodes.procedure: The cleaned Ni foam was immersed in a mixed aqueous solution of Co(NO3)2 (0.09M) urea (0.285M) and NH4F. Then, the reaction precursors were transferred into Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 10h, generating CCH nanoarrays on Ni foam.
nodes.source_text: the cleaned Ni foam was immersed in a mixed aqueous solution of Co(NO3)2 (0.09M) urea (0.285M) and NH4F. Then, the reaction precursors were transferred into Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 10h

nodes.name: ZIF-67 formation
nodes.procedure: the resultant CCH was immersed in 2.0M 2-methylimidazole solution containing 5mL of H2O and 5mL of EtOH for 15h at room temperature, forming ZIF-67 on the top of CCH nanoneedle arrays (denoted as CCH/ZIF-67).
nodes.source_text: the resultant CCH was immersed in 2.0M 2-methylimidazole solution containing 5mL of H2O and 5mL of EtOH 15h at room temperature

nodes.name: Sn-doping via ion exchange
nodes.procedure: the resultant CCH/ZIF-67 sample was immersed into a 20mL of 0.002M Na2SnO3 solution, which was transferred to Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and kept at 80°C for 1h. During this step, the formed CCH/ZIF-67 underwent an ion exchange process between Co²⁺ and Sn⁴⁺, resulting in the formation of Sn-doped CCH/ZIF-67 (denoted Sn-CCH/ZIF-67).
nodes.source_text: the resultant CCH/ZIF-67 sample was immersed into a 20mL of 0.002M Na2SnO3 solution... kept at 80°C for 1h

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: as-obtained Sn-CCH/ZIF-67 and 2.0g of NaH2PO2 were placed in two separate alumina boats with NaH2PO2 at the upstream side of the tube furnace. The furnace was maintained at 350°C for 2h under Ar flow, generating the Sn4P3/Co2P SCNAs.
nodes.source_text: as-obtained Sn-CCH/ZIF-67 and 2.0g of NaH2PO2 were placed in two separate alumina boats... maintained at 350°C for 2h under Ar flow

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows high density vertically aligned needle-like nanoarrays covering Ni foam with stalk length ~8 μm and diameter 150 nm, and shapeless rough-surface caps grafted on top.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The panoramic scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image of the as-derived Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs in Fig. 2a suggests that the surface of the Ni foam substrate is entirely covered by a high density of vertically aligned needle-like nanoarrays... the average length and diameter of the 'stalks' are measured to be ∼8 μm and 150 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms featureless morphology of caps and hetero-structured feature of both caps and stalks in Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical TEM image of the Sn₄P₃/Co₂P 'caps' (Fig. 2d) verifies their featureless morphology... the TEM image (Fig. 2g), HRTEM image (Fig. 2h) and FFT diffraction patterns (Fig. 2i) of the Sn₄P₃/Co₂P 'stalk' collectively demonstrate the hetero-structured feature of the 'stalk'.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals heterointerfaces between Sn₄P₃ and Co₂P in caps with lattice fringes of 0.221 nm for Co₂P (111) and 0.284 nm for Sn₄P₃ (107); similar heterostructure confirmed in stalks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2e) clearly manifests the existence of well-defined heterointerfaces between Sn₄P₃ and Co₂P components... The measured lattice fringes with spacings of 0.221 and 0.284 nm are corresponding to the interplanar distances of Co₂P (111) and Sn₄P₃ (107) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Sn, P, and O throughout Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs caps and stalks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images and the elemental mapping analyses (Fig. S7) of the Sn₄P₃/Co₂P 'caps' and 'stalk' suggest the uniform distribution of Co, Sn, P, and O throughout the entire Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms coexistence of hexagonal Co₂P (JCPDS #54-0413) and rhombohedral Sn₄P₃ (JCPDF #20-1294) phases in Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs with no residual CCH or ZIF-67 peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The heterostructural composition of the as-prepared Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs was further testified by the XRD pattern (Fig. 3a), which suggests the coexistence of hexagonal Co₂P (JCPDS #54-0413) and rhombohedral Sn₄P₃ (JCPDF #20-1294).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms surface composition of Co, Sn, P, O in Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs. Co 2p peaks at 778.2 eV (Co-P), 781.7 eV (Co-O), 792.6 eV (Co-P), 798.1 eV (Co-O) with ~0.4 eV negative shift vs Co₂P SCNAs indicating Sn₄P₃/Co₂P electronic interaction. Sn 3d₅/₂ at 485.2, 487.1 eV and 3d₃/₂ at 494.5, 495.2 eV. P 2p at 129.2 eV (P 2p₃/₂), 130.2 eV (P 2p₁/₂), 134.3 eV (oxidized P). O 1s shows adsorbed water (530.5 eV), hydroxy oxygen (531.3 eV), metal-oxide (532.3 eV), pyrophosphates (532.9 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey of spectrum (Fig. 3b) indicates that the surface of Sn₄P₃/Co₂P SCNAs is composed of Co, Sn, P, and O elements. Fig. 3c displays the high-resolution Co 2p spectra... binding energies of Co 2p exhibit a negative shift of ∼0.4 eV... The high-resolution Sn 3d spectrum (Fig. 3d)... P 2p spectrum (Fig. 3e)... O 1s spectrum (Fig. 3f).
